heads.la: B. HIERONYMI PROLOGUS DUPLEX IN LIBRUM JOB.
heads.en: THE TWOFOLD PROLOGUE OF BLESSED JEROME ON THE BOOK OF JOB.
PROTHEMATA ON JOB. [n: (Ex Greg. in Job, passim.)]

headnotes.la: Quaedam historice hic dicuntur, et allegorice, et moraliter. Quaedam nequeunt ad litteram accipi; quia erronea essent vel impossibilia, vel a se invicem discordantia, ut illud scilicet
headnotes.en: …ere are said historically, and allegorically, and morally. Some cannot be taken according to the letter, because they would be erroneous or impossible, or at variance one with another: as that, namely

headnotes.la: quasi gigantes mundum vehant; et illud scilicet
headnotes.en: as though giants carried the world; and that, namely

headnotes.la: quasi tam patiens velit suspendio vitam finire: et illud scilicet
headnotes.en: as though one so patient would wish to end his life by hanging; and that, namely

headnotes.la: etc. Aliquando qui sensum litterae negligit, veritatis lumen sibi abscondit, dum intrinsecus aliud quaerendo, quod foris est perdit; ut dum de misericordiae operibus dicit
headnotes.en: …lects the sense of the letter hides from himself the light of truth, while by seeking something else within he loses what lies without; as when, speaking of the works of mercy, he seeks an allegory in

headnotes.la: Erranti homini data est lex. Inobediens legi confunditur exemplo, maxime hominis sine lege, qui legaliter vixit. Unde [n: (Isa. XXIII)]
headnotes.en: To erring man the law was given. He who is disobedient to the law is put to shame by the example, chiefly of a man without the law who lived lawfully. Whence [n: (Isa. XXIII)]

headnotes.la: id est, stabilitas in lege positorum,
headnotes.en: that is, the stability of those set under the law,

headnotes.la: …is de se quasi de aliis loqui: Spiritus enim est qui loquitur in ipsis sicut de aliis. Unde angelus Moysi, modo angelus dicitur, qui exterius servit, modo Dominus qui interius praesidet; unde et David
headnotes.en: … of others. For it is the Spirit who speaks in them as concerning others. Whence the angel of Moses is now called an angel, who serves outwardly, now the Lord, who presides inwardly; whence David also

headnotes.la: …Deo: sed flagellis commota, ut aromata nobis redolet. Unde et fideles grano sinapis comparantur, quod non contritum lene est, sed si conteritur inardescit, et quod latebat in eo prodit; unde in Psalmo
headnotes.en: …rance to us like spices. Whence the faithful too are compared to a grain of mustard, which unbruised is mild, but if it is bruised grows hot, and what lay hidden in it comes forth; whence in the Psalm

headnotes.la: …a Ecclesia et hic pro laboribus suis duplicia accipit, dum susceptis gentibus, in fine et Judaeos convertit, et in futuro duplici stola dotabitur, id est, beatitudine animae et corporis. Unde Propheta
headnotes.en: …ntiles having been received, at the end she converts the Jews also; and in the world to come she will be endowed with a double robe, that is, with the beatitude of soul and of body. Whence the Prophet

headnotes.la: Afflicto Job dicitur: sed quanto tempore fuerit, tacetur; quia Ecclesia affligenda scitur, sed quandiu ignoratur; unde
headnotes.en: …d *Afflictus*, "Job is said to be afflicted"]; but for how long a time it was, is passed over in silence, because the Church is known to be destined for affliction, but for how long is unknown; whence

headnotes.la: [n: (ID., ibid.)] Prius persona apta describitur quam pugna ejus dicatur, ut talis posse vincere videatur
headnotes.en: [n: (ID., ibid.)] The person is first described as fitting, before his combat is told, so that such a one may be seen able to conquer

headnotes.la: id est, inter angelos orienti luci inhaerentes, magni sumus, eorum socii. Orientales sunt omnes qui per fidem sunt in Christo, de quo Propheta
headnotes.en: that is, among the angels that cleave to the rising light, we are great, their fellows. Orientals are all who by faith are in Christ, of whom the Prophet

headnotes.la: …cibum debriantur, dum contemplationis rore infundi appetunt. Sed ex ipsis bonis et mala oriuntur, ut elatio; vel cum pro his laetitia fit menti, adest etiam quaedam securitas, inde torpor. Ergo subdit
headnotes.en: …t out of these very good things evils also arise, such as elation; or when gladness comes to the mind on account of them, a certain security is also present, and thence sluggishness. Therefore he adds

headnotes.la: Quia bonis Dei cogitationibus quae ex Deo sunt, se interserit ut perturbet, sed eum latentem nobis Deus detegit. Unde dicitur
headnotes.en: Because he thrusts himself in among the good thoughts of God which are from God, that he may disturb them; but God uncovers him to us when he lies hidden. Whence it is said

headnotes.la: quod dicere, est ejus insidias aperire nobis
headnotes.en: which to say is to lay open his snares to us

headnotes.la: Carnalia corda scrutatur, ut mala inserat; nec transvolat, sed perambulat, quia non cito deserit quem tentat, sed moratur, ut vestigia pravitatis imprimat: contra eum Job laudatur
headnotes.en: … sow evils in them; nor does he fly over, but walks through, because he does not quickly forsake the one he tempts, but tarries, that he may imprint the traces of depravity. Against him Job is praised

headnotes.la: quem Deus bonum facit, et roborat, quasi in auribus Satanae laudat: unde ipse gravius contra saevit, dicens
headnotes.en: whom God makes good and strengthens, and praises as it were in the ears of Satan. Whence he rages the more grievously against him, saying

headnotes.la: …t, mens aliquantulum erigitur, quasi bona a se: quae bona diabolus appetit male: sed Deus tentari bene sinit, ut dum in bonis illis homo concutitur, imbecillitate cognita in Deo solidetur. Unde subdit
headnotes.en: …ese good things the devil desires for evil, but God permits the testing for good, so that while man is shaken in those good things, his weakness being known, he may be made firm in God. Whence he adds

headnotes.la: [n: (GREC.)] Non quaerit a bonis, quia non quaerimus nisi quod nescimus, et Dei nescire est reprobare, ut et bonus vir nescire mentiri dicitur, non quod nesciat, sed quod contemnat. Dicere ergo
headnotes.en: …ask save what we do not know; and for God not to know is to reprobate, just as a good man too is said not to know how to lie, not because he does not know, but because he contemns it. To say therefore

headnotes.la: …imus nisi quod nescimus, et Dei nescire est reprobare, ut et bonus vir nescire mentiri dicitur, non quod nesciat, sed quod contemnat. Dicere ergo « unde venis? vias ejus est quasi incognitas reprobare
headnotes.en: … as a good man too is said not to know how to lie, not because he does not know, but because he contemns it. To say therefore « whence comest thou? is to reprobate his ways as though they were unknown

headnotes.la: …erram circumivit, qui in coelo quietus non stetit: et non transvolat, sed perambulat, quia a spiritualis potentiae volatu corruit, pressus nimis gravedine suae malitiae. De membris quoque ejus dicitur
headnotes.en: …rest in heaven; and he does not fly over but walks through, because he fell from the flight of spiritual power, weighed down too heavily by the burden of his own malice. Of his members also it is said

headnotes.la: …olus venisse redemptorem senserat, sed, propter humilia quae passus est, quidquid de deitate suspicatus est, ei in dubium evenit pro sua superbia, et non Deum natum, sed Dei gratia custoditum credidit
headnotes.en: …ly things which he suffered, whatever he had suspected concerning his deity came into doubt for him by reason of his own pride, and he believed him not to be God born, but one kept by the grace of God

headnotes.la: …center gerit: sed innocens non esset si inter adversa staret: quia nequit in die, in nocte adversorum, vult reprobare. Non ergo vires Job, sed quemque verius adversis probare sciens, tentandum expetit
headnotes.en: … in the day, he wishes to reprove him in the night of adversities. Therefore, knowing that by adversities he would prove not the strength of Job, but each man more truly, he demands that he be tempted

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Non petitione diaboli provocatus Deus vincitur, sed hosti concedit ad dolorem et deceptionem suam quod famulo prosit
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] God is not overcome, provoked by the devil's petition, but grants to the enemy, unto the enemy's own grief and deception, what may profit his servant

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Per passiones peccare posse Christum putavit
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] He thought that through sufferings Christ could sin

headnotes.la: Id est, ad desiderii sui vota pervenit. Vel egreditur, dum quod bona intentione sibi permittitur, prava intentione ab eo perpetratur
headnotes.en: That is, he came to the desires of his own longing. Or he goes forth when what is permitted him with a good intention is carried out by him with a depraved intention

headnotes.la: Quo exiit, ab eo qui ubique est? sed quamdiu pressus potentia Dei, Satan quod appetiit, exercere non potuit, quasi ante faciem stetit; exit cum laxatus est ad effectum sui desiderii
headnotes.en: …? But so long as, pressed down by the power of God, Satan could not carry out what he desired, he stood as it were before his face; he goes out when he is let loose to the accomplishment of his desire

headnotes.la: VERS. 13.-- « Cum autem quadam die filii et
headnotes.en: VERS. 13.-- « Now when on a certain day the sons and

headnotes.la: …neratus; minor, Gentilis in fine vocatus. In domo ergo primogeniti, apostoli convivantur: quia adhuc Scripturae sacrae deliciis in collectione solius Judaici populi vescebantur, quibus tunc dictum est
headnotes.en: …e end. In the house therefore of the firstborn the apostles feast, because as yet they fed on the delights of sacred Scripture within the gathering of the Jewish people alone, to whom it was then said

headnotes.la: …rum pascuntur. Sabaei captivantes, id est daemones, pueros, id est incipientes, nondum virilis constantiae, gladio, id est desperatione aeternitatis. Nuntius qui evadit, propheticus sermo est: qui ait
headnotes.en: …g captive, that is, demons; the boys, that is, beginners, not yet of manly steadfastness; with the sword, that is, with despair of eternity. The messenger who escapes is the prophetic word, which says

headnotes.la: [n: (GREG.)], Filii et filiae (ut dictum est) sunt apostoli et plebes subditae, qui in Judaea Scriptura vescebantur
headnotes.en: [n: (GREG.)], The sons and daughters (as has been said) are the apostles and the peoples subject to them, who in Judaea fed upon Scripture

headnotes.la: …s stat domus, sacerdotes, scribas, seniores populi, Pharisaeos, commovit. Domus, id est, Judaea in persecutione Domini cadens apostolos in desperatione obruit. Et verus est sermo de persecutore populo
headnotes.en: …the elders of the people, the Pharisees. The house, that is, Judaea, falling in the persecution of the Lord, overwhelmed the apostles in despair. And the word concerning the persecuting people is true

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Ruente domo, etc., *usque ad* ut totum cor in Dei amore ardens eas devotionis perfectione consumat
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] The house falling, etc., *as far as* that the whole heart, burning in the love of God, may consume them by the perfection of devotion

headnotes.la: Magna constantia putatur, etc., *usque ad* et se divinae potentiae consentire ostenderet
headnotes.en: It is thought a great steadfastness, etc., *as far as* and might show that he consented to the divine power

headnotes.la: [n: (GREG.)] Cadens adoravit, quia ille veram orationem exhibet, qui quod pulvis sit humiliter videt. Unde et dicit
headnotes.en: [n: (GREG.)] Falling, he adored, because he offers true prayer who humbly sees that he is dust. Whence he also says

headnotes.la: …redens Synagoga, adulterino complexu eum constringere voluit: cui tegmen litterae reliquit, et se conspicuum Gentibus praebuit. Sed nudus revertetur, cum in fine mundi reliquiis Israel Deus innotescet
headnotes.en: …embrace; to whom he left the covering of the letter, and showed himself openly to the Gentiles. But he will return naked, when at the end of the world God shall be made known to the remnants of Israel

headnotes.la: Judaea dum venturum credidit, abstulit, cum ipsa venientem contempsit
headnotes.en: Judaea, while it believed that he was to come, took [him] away when she herself despised him at his coming

headnotes.la: … quasi quae extra se sunt, dolore propriae carnis tentat, quasi pro se doleat, qui non pro aliis. Hoc cum fieri petit, dicit desideriis; haec et per membra verbis et desideriis intulit, per quae dixit
headnotes.en: …rieve for himself who does not grieve for others. When he asks that this be done, he speaks with desires; and these things he brought in through his members by words and desires, through which he said

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Pellis pro pelle datur, quia saepe, dum ictus contra oculum venit, manum opponimus, ut potius in ipsa quam in teneriori vulneremur: hoc consuete fieri sciens, dicit
headnotes.en: …for skin, because often, when a blow comes against the eye, we put the hand in the way, that we may be wounded rather in it than in the more tender part. Knowing that this is customarily done, he says

headnotes.la: Quasi, ideo Job extra se tot flagella aequanimiter sustinet, quia ne ipse feriatur, pavet: et cura sui minus de suis sentit; unde ipsum ferire expetit
headnotes.en: …with an even mind so many scourges outside himself, because he is afraid lest he himself be struck; and out of care for himself he feels less about his own. Whence he demands to strike the man himself

headnotes.la: Saepe diabolus, postquam mentem impugnavit, ad tempus cessat, ut securam repente irrumpat: ideo iterum Job expetit, quod Deus ei reticendo concedit
headnotes.en: Often the devil, after he has assaulted the mind, ceases for a time, that he may suddenly break in upon it while it is secure. Therefore he demands Job again, which God grants him by keeping silence

headnotes.la: …os et ei electos a jure suo amittit, cum illum occidit a planta pedis usque ad verticem: quia ab exordio mundi membris ejus dura intulit, et usque ad caput ipsorum, id est Christum, saeviendo pervenit
headnotes.en: …he slays him from the sole of the foot even to the crown: because from the beginning of the world he brought hard things upon his members, and by his raging reached even to their head, that is, Christ

headnotes.la: …erna cupit, quasi dicat: Quid simpliciter aeterna petis et super his male gemis, excidens (aeterna despice) et mala praesentia, vel moriens evade. Sed haec passi sunt illi forma rectitudinis. Unde ait
headnotes.en: … eternal things and groan grievously over these, falling away (despise eternal things) and escape present evils, or by dying. But those men suffered these things, a form of uprightness. Whence he says

headnotes.la: ferientes extra sustinent, perversos intus docent: ibi fortes, hic misericordes: ibi adversos repeliunt, hic suos protegunt; et grande est in acie hoc utrumque facere
headnotes.en: …ike without, they teach the perverse within: there strong, here merciful; there they drive back adversaries, here they protect their own; and it is a great thing to do both of these in the battle line

headnotes.la: Eva verba sua repetit, quasi dicens: Desere simplicitatem, id est, obedientiam, vetitum comedendo contemne
headnotes.en: Eve repeats her own words, as if saying: Forsake simplicity, that is, obedience; contemn the forbidden thing by eating it

headnotes.la: [n: (GREG.)] Quia sensus, non sexus in vitio est: non ait una de mulieribus, sed
headnotes.en: [n: (GREG.)] Because the understanding, not the sex, is in fault: he does not say, one of the women, but

headnotes.la: quod pravum sapit, accidentis stultitiae est, non conditione naturae
headnotes.en: what savours of depravity belongs to accidental folly, not by the condition of nature

headnotes.la: … malis bonorum reminisci, ne sit omnimoda desperatio, sicut in laetis temperat ab elatione praevisio mali. Unde dicitur: In die bonorum ne sis immemor malorum, et in die malorum ne sis immemor bonorum
headnotes.en: …e, just as in glad times the foresight of evil tempers one from elation. Whence it is said: In the day of good things be not unmindful of evils, and in the day of evils be not unmindful of good things

headnotes.la: id est, si ad aeterna bona tendimus, cur non mala praesentia sustinemus?
headnotes.en: that is, if we strive toward eternal good things, why do we not endure present evils?

headnotes.la: …ra suadentem recta reticuit. Patientiam habuit, Deo gratias agens, insipientiam conjugis arguendo docens . et sic victus ardentius hostis instigatur, et quia uxor tacuit alios excitavit ad contumelias
headnotes.en: …tience, giving thanks to God, teaching by reproof the folly of his wife . And so the enemy, being conquered, is the more hotly goaded; and because the wife fell silent, he stirred up others to insults

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Amici haereticos significant, etc., *usque ad* hypocritae nolentes esse, sed videri docti
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] The friends signify heretics, etc., *as far as* hypocrites, not wishing to be, but to seem, learned

headnotes.la: Non dicit audientes, ideo quod vitia haec audiant, sed diabolus qui per ista tentat haec intelligit
headnotes.en: He does not say hearing because these vices hear, but the devil, who tempts by these things, understands them

headnotes.la: …ocent, quasi consolantur. Vere autem consolantur in afflictione praesenti, qui de aeternis erudiunt. Haeretici amici nominantur, quia non ex sua nequitia, sed ex nostra benignitate nominandi sunt: ut,
headnotes.en: … But they truly console in present affliction who instruct concerning eternal things. Heretics are called friends, because they are to be named not from their own wickedness but from our kindness: as,

headnotes.la: Qui in imo sunt oculos levant, etc., *usque ad* quasi hostes per intentionis hostiam in amicos mutamus
headnotes.en: They who are below lift up their eyes, etc., *as far as* we change enemies as it were into friends by the sacrifice of our intention

headnotes.la: …eis videt. Videndum tamen est consolatori, ne nimis dolens afflictum gravet, et dolentem desperare faciat: forsitan amici Job nimis doluerunt, nescientes mentem percussi, quasi ille a corde cecidisset
headnotes.en: …t, grieving too much, he weigh down the afflicted and make the mourner despair. Perhaps Job's friends grieved too much, not knowing the mind of the stricken man, as though he had fallen from his heart

headnotes.la: …nt. Vel terra est incarnatio Christi, quam quidam haeretici non negant, sed vel de deitate, vel de incarnationis qualitate discordant a nobis: quia ergo illam non negant, quasi cum Job in terra sedent
headnotes.en: …certain heretics do not deny, but they disagree with us either about the deity or about the manner of the incarnation; because therefore they do not deny it, they sit as it were with Job on the ground

headnotes.la: Ignoratur utrum continue, an tot diebus crebra visitatione insisterent
headnotes.en: It is not known whether they persisted continuously, or over so many days with frequent visitation

headnotes.la: Quia vel in hoc, quod vere, vel in hoc quod stulte sapiunt, incarnationi non contradicunt
headnotes.en: Because either in that which they rightly, or in that which they foolishly, understand, they do not contradict the incarnation

headnotes.la: …cis. Cum ergo patienter in omnibus gratias egit et bene docuit, nunc nullo instigante non est credendus ex impatientia ad maledictionem prorumpere, sed quietus hoc dicit, quia inter mala laudavit Deum
headnotes.en: …ave thanks in all things and taught well, he is not now, with none instigating him, to be believed to break out into cursing from impatience; but he says this calmly, because amid evils he praised God

headnotes.la: etc. [n: (Ibid.)] Id est, exordio delectationis, ad quem finem perditionis rapit, videatur, et per poenitentiam crucietur. Quod si ita punita est
headnotes.en: etc. [n: (Ibid.)] That is, let it be seen, at the outset of delight, to what end of perdition it hurries a man, and let it be tormented by penitence. But if it has been so punished

headnotes.la: In judicio ut puniat; et non illustrabit. Illustrat lumine, qui arguit: sed quasi tegitur, qui in memoria judicis non revocatur. Unde
headnotes.en: In judgment, that he may punish; and he will not illumine. He illumines with light who reproves; but he is as it were covered who is not recalled into the memory of the judge. Whence

headnotes.la: Id est, diem delectationis, ne ab eo qui omnia videt, videatur
headnotes.en: That is, the day of delight, lest it be seen by him who sees all things

headnotes.la: [n: (GREG.)] Id est, lamenta poenitentiae vel occulta Dei judicia, a quibus praeveniente gratia absolvimur, quam nos mereri nescimus
headnotes.en: [n: (GREG.)] That is, the laments of penitence, or the hidden judgments of God, from which we are absolved by prevenient grace, which we know not how to merit

headnotes.la: Id est, mors Christi secundum carnem, etc., *usque ad* in quo misericordia subvenit, hoc homo puniat: unde sequitur
headnotes.en: That is, the death of Christ according to the flesh, etc., *as far as* in what mercy has succoured him, let man punish it. Whence follows

headnotes.la: Id est, mentis confusio, de qua dicitur
headnotes.en: That is, the confusion of the mind, of which it is said

headnotes.la: Quasi turbo tempestatis est concitatus, etc., *usque ad* pro caecitate damnationis in qua nati sumus
headnotes.en: It is as it were a whirlwind of a storm stirred up, etc., *as far as* for the blindness of the damnation in which we were born

headnotes.la: Quia a frequentia illa separatur, vel hominem, quem sibi socium fecerat, amittit: et electis per gratiam redemptis solus cum corpore suo gehennae traditur
headnotes.en: Because it is separated from that throng, or loses the man whom it had made its companion; and when the elect have been redeemed by grace, he alone with his own body is handed over to Gehenna

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] In veteri translatione, etc., *usque ad* et in fine solutus aperte bella gerat
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] In the old translation, etc., *as far as* and at the end, being loosed, may openly wage wars

headnotes.la: … Hae sunt quae cauda draconis, id est, extrema persecutione Antichristi, trahuntur; hae obtenebrantur, quia malitia hostis sic praevalet eis, ut apertis malis involvantur, quales intus, tales exterius
headnotes.en: …dragon, that is, by the last persecution of Antichrist; these are darkened, because the malice of the enemy so prevails over them that they are wrapped in open evils, such outwardly as they are within

headnotes.la: Hoc secundum membra ejus, etc., *usque ad* quae Christum prophetando sustinuit, sed venientem non cognovit
headnotes.en: This according to his members, etc., *as far as* which by prophesying waited for Christ, but did not know him when he came

headnotes.la: Non est credendum, etc., *usque ad* ne ad delectationem suggestio traheret
headnotes.en: It is not to be believed, etc., *as far as* lest suggestion should draw him to delight

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Per nunc, quod est praesentis temporis, stantem semper in praesenti, id est, aeternam quietem designat
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] By "now," which belongs to present time, he designates the rest that stands always in the present, that is, eternal rest

headnotes.la: …ccaret, illuc etiam non redemptus ascenderet, ad quod apostoli et sancti praedicatores post redemptionem cum magno labore perveniunt, qui non differuntur ut antiqui, sed mox post mortem intrant coelum
headnotes.en: …ve ascended thither even unredeemed, whither the apostles and holy preachers after the redemption arrive with great labour, who are not deferred as the ancients were, but soon after death enter heaven

headnotes.la: …tres secundo mortuos protulit, quasi uterus abortivi fuit: et ipsi quasi ab utero mortui sunt, qui sine tabulis legis Deum naturaliter timuerunt, et futurum redemptorem credentes voluptates occiderunt
headnotes.en: …s it were the womb of an untimely birth; and they were as it were dead from the womb, who without the tables of the law feared God by nature, and believing in the Redeemer to come slew their pleasures

headnotes.la: Id est, in luce Christi, quam antiqui praestolati sunt, Gentiles a turba desideriorum mundi cessant, et tranquilla mente jam aeternam quietem praegustant. Et hoc est
headnotes.en: That is, in the light of Christ, which the ancients awaited, the Gentiles cease from the throng of the desires of the world, and with tranquil mind already foretaste eternal rest. And this is

headnotes.la: In mundo fortes robore, non fessi dicuntur. Qui vero in amore Dei roboratur, salubriter a sua virtute deficit, et quo fortius aeterna petit, eo magis fessus, in terrenis moritur. Unde
headnotes.en: …earied. But he who is strengthened in the love of God healthfully fails from his own strength; and the more strongly he seeks eternal things, the more wearied he is, and dies to earthly things. Whence

headnotes.la: …loriae filiorum Dei solventur. Vide gradus: impii conversi cessant; exercitati in intimo sinu quiescunt; a vinculis corruptionis absoluti ad libertatem perveniunt. Sed quid hic interim egerint, subdit
headnotes.en: …ee the degrees: the wicked, being converted, cease; the well-exercised rest in the inmost bosom; those absolved from the chains of corruption come to liberty. But what they did here meanwhile, he adds

headnotes.la: …tur. Vide gradus: impii conversi cessant; exercitati in intimo sinu quiescunt; a vinculis corruptionis absoluti ad libertatem perveniunt. Sed quid hic interim egerint, subdit: « Qui non audierunt, etc
headnotes.en: … being converted, cease; the well-exercised rest in the inmost bosom; those absolved from the chains of corruption come to liberty. But what they did here meanwhile, he adds: « Who have not heard, etc

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Quia hic est discretio operum, ibi erit dignitatum. Unde
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] Because here there is a distinction of works, there it will be of dignities. Whence

headnotes.la: [n: (GREG. in lib. Job lib. V.)] Contemplatus requiem, ubi liber a Domino despicit saeculi prospera, quae ab ea retrahunt
headnotes.en: [n: (GREG. in lib. Job lib. V.)] Having contemplated that rest, where, made free by the Lord, he looks down upon the prosperities of the world, which draw men back from it

headnotes.la: id est, prosperitas in peregrinationis miseria: quia, si non justum penitus opprimit, tamen mentem in amorem Dei et in dispensatione sui dividit; unde addit
headnotes.en: …prosperity in the wretchedness of our pilgrimage: because, although it does not utterly crush the just man, yet it divides the mind between the love of God and the management of itself. Whence he adds

headnotes.la: …tioni: et sic et multis prosunt, et quo se imperfectos vident, per humilitatem amplius surgunt: et quod a desideriis differuntur, ipsa tarditate ad eadem dilatantur: unde addit, quasi effodientes, etc
headnotes.en: …lves imperfect, they rise the higher through humility: and in that they are put off from their desires, by that very delay they are enlarged toward the same: whence he adds, as though digging out, etc

headnotes.la: Flent enim, quia deseri se timent: et ne pia percussio non sit disciplinae, sed vindictae, unde
headnotes.en: For they weep, because they fear to be forsaken: and lest the godly stroke be not of discipline, but of vengeance, whence
[n: (GREG.)] After he had admonished him kindly, he openly rebukes him

headnotes.en: that is, the severity and terror of Job himself

headnotes.la: …rsu hujus vitae a saecularibus rebus oculos claudit quod ad concupiscendum culpa primis parentibus aperuit. Et nemo ad videnda interna perducitur, nisi ab his quae exterius implicant subtrahatur; unde
headnotes.en: …o worldly things, which fault opened to our first parents for coveting. And no man is brought to the seeing of inward things unless he be withdrawn from those things which entangle him without; whence

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Pili sunt superflua quaelibet humanae corruptionis cogitationes vitae veteris: quas si a mente excludimus, pilos carne incidimus, ut non dolore fatigemur. Unde Moyses
headnotes.en: ….)] The hairs are all the superfluous thoughts of human corruption, of the old life: which if we shut out from the mind, we cut the hairs from the flesh, that we be not wearied with pain. Whence Moses

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Vel mane, prosperitas; vespera, adversitas; sed per utrumque pereunt, quia per prospera lascivi, per adversa impatientes ad insaniam surgunt. Et quia nullus eorum, scilicet,
headnotes.en: …r morning is prosperity; evening, adversity; but by both they perish, because through prosperity they are wanton, through adversity impatient, and rise up to madness. And because none of them, namely,

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Quoniam hoc veraciter contra iniquos protulit, quamvis latenter Job in numero eorum proposuerit: fastu sapientiae inflatus apertam irrisionem in Job subdit
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] Since he had truly brought this forth against the wicked, though he had secretly set Job in their number, being puffed up with the pride of wisdom he adds an open mockery against Job

headnotes.la: id est, si afflictus clames, Deus non respondet, id est non dat effectum, quia in tranquillitate eum contempsisti; et
headnotes.en: that is, if in affliction thou criest out, God does not answer, that is, he does not give effect, because in tranquillity thou didst despise him; and

headnotes.la: Habet quisque donum intelligentiae, quo recta intelligit et dicit: Sed quia eadem non amat nec facit, a messe quam habet, jejunat; sed qui esurit justitiam ab illo audiens recta, se reficit, unde
headnotes.en: …things and speaks them: but because he neither loves nor does the same, he fasts from the harvest which he has; but he who hungers for justice, hearing right things from him, refreshes himself, whence

headnotes.la: Quia inde ille justius de negligentia punitur, iste de studio coronatur. Sed quia ad intelligendum recta non modo studio, sed et persecutionibus erudimur, additum
headnotes.en: …e is more justly punished for negligence, the other crowned for diligence. But because we are schooled to the understanding of right things not only by diligence, but also by persecutions, it is added

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Humus, id est, elementa mundi in poenam vertuntur delinquentium; unde dicitur
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] The ground, that is, the elements of the world, are turned into the punishment of them that offend; whence it is said

headnotes.la: Quia impossibile est in hac peregrinatione sine labore esse: sed in eo quod caro affligitur, mens ad petenda alta levatur
headnotes.en: Because it is impossible in this pilgrimage to be without labor: but in that the flesh is afflicted, the mind is lifted to the seeking of high things

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Haec verba mystica sunt, quia amici Job societate ejus eruditi erant
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] These words are mystical, because Job's friends had been schooled by his fellowship

headnotes.la: …ius, alia permittit iratus: quae tunc in usum sui consilii vertit, ut quae ejus consilio repugnant, ejus consilio militent; et quod sine ejus voluntate geritur, ejus voluntati contrarium non sit, unde
headnotes.en: …y: which things he then turns to the use of his own counsel, so that the things which fight against his counsel serve his counsel; and what is done without his will is not contrary to his will, whence

headnotes.la: Palpando quaerimus quae oculis non videmus: Judaei miracula viderant, et adhuc quasi palpantes quaerebant
headnotes.en: By groping we seek the things we do not see with the eyes: the Jews had seen the miracles, and still as it were groping they were seeking

headnotes.la: …raesentis vitae et adjutoria Dei. Fames mentis est silentium verbi Dei: quo subtracto, tentatio carnis invalescit, quae est bellum. Sed Deus etiam in fame a morte animam eripit, quia verbo suo reficit
headnotes.en: …he silence of the word of God: which being withdrawn, the temptation of the flesh grows strong, which is war. But God even in famine snatches the soul from death, because he refreshes it with his word

headnotes.la: Id est, ab exprobratione contumeliae, propter quam irrisus a bono cessat; unde David
headnotes.en: That is, from the upbraiding of reproach, for which, being mocked, he ceases from good; whence David

headnotes.la: Ab hac sanctus absconditur, quia, dum hic laudem non quaerit, nec contumelias sentit; sed, quia post haec aliquis cruciatus corporum timet, sequitur
headnotes.en: From this the holy man is hidden, because, while he seeks not praise here, neither does he feel reproaches; but because after these things a man fears some torment of bodies, there follows

headnotes.la: Vastitas e s gehenna quae foris, etc., *usque ad* ut in articulo mortis ejus impetus non horreat, subditur
headnotes.en: The wasting is [sic: *e s*] the gehenna which is without, etc., *as far as* that in the moment of death he may not shudder at its onset, there is added

headnotes.la: …ur. Qui ergo recte vivit pacto se lapidibus jungit: quia in eo quod mundum deserit, sanctis per imitationem se alligat; unde impugnatio crescit, qua tamen attritus humilius Deo subditur, unde subjicit
headnotes.en: … because in that he forsakes the world, he binds himself to the saints by imitation; whence assault grows, by which nevertheless, being worn down, he is more humbly made subject to God, whence he adds

headnotes.la: …cum plene Deo subdimur, verbo praedicationis replemur. Ante liberi sacro eloquio pasti; et tamen ad quaedam quae in mundo petimus vacantes. Ex praedicatione, magna proles fidelium sequitur. Et hoc est
headnotes.en: …being free, they were fed with the sacred eloquence; and yet they were at leisure for certain things which we seek in the world. Out of preaching a great offspring of the faithful follows. And this is

headnotes.la: VERS. 26.-- « Ingredieris in abundantia sepulcrum. [n: (Ibid.)] Sepulcrum est contemplatio, etc., *usque ad* quod utilitati proximorum refundant
headnotes.en: VERS. 26.-- « Thou shalt enter into the grave in abundance. [n: (Ibid.)] The grave is contemplation, etc., *as far as* what they may pour back for the profit of their neighbors

headnotes.la: In hoc notat se, non secundum superficiem dixisse supra sepulcrum, bestias, lapides, tabernaculum, et hujusmodi, sed in his interiora quaesisse
headnotes.en: In this he notes of himself that he had not spoken according to the surface concerning the grave, the beasts, the stones, the tabernacle, and the like, but that he had sought inward things in them

headnotes.la: Tactus flagellis verbis lacessitur, non ut non erectus in defensionem contumax caderet: sed ut percussus tacens gratias egit, lacessitus recta respondit
headnotes.en: Touched by the scourges, he is provoked by words, not that, not raised up into his own defence, he might fall defiant: but that, struck, he kept silence and gave thanks, and provoked, answered rightly

headnotes.la: [n: (GREG.)] Id est, elationem compescit, ut dicat
headnotes.en: [n: (GREG.)] That is, it curbs pride, so that he may say

headnotes.la: id est, mala saeculi jam sunt dulces cibi prae amore coeli. Et cum haec dulcia sint,
headnotes.en: that is, the evils of the world are now sweet food before the love of heaven. And since these are sweet,

headnotes.la: [n: (GREG. in Job lib. VII.)] Conterit adversarius, et defecit a te homo. Conterit Deus, et fractus a vitiis in virtute solidatur. Qui ergo per flagella Deo appropriare desiderat, dicit
headnotes.en: …. VII.)] The adversary crushes, and man falls away from thee. God crushes, and one broken off from his vices is made solid in virtue. He therefore who through scourges desires to draw near to God says

headnotes.la: Si exterius despectus, intus solio judicii praesidet; nam ad sententias erumpit
headnotes.en: Though despised without, within he presides on the throne of judgment; for he breaks out into sentences

headnotes.la: …t, separabuntur. Mali aeterna non intelligunt, nisi cum jam pro terrenis puniuntur: tunc mens aestuat, et igne serae poenitentiae se inflammat; tunc ejus duritia per supplicium liquatur, unde propheta
headnotes.en: …rnal things, save when they are already punished for earthly ones: then the mind boils, and inflames itself with the fire of late repentance; then its hardness is melted by torment, whence the prophet

headnotes.la: Quia nihil secum de fructu sui laboris portant. Sed justus in conspectu Domini non apparet vacuus: portat enim manipulos justitiae. Ab illorum autem imitatione per finem terret,
headnotes.en: …othing with them of the fruit of their labour. But the just man does not appear empty in the sight of the Lord: for he carries the sheaves of justice. And from imitating them he terrifies by their end

headnotes.la: …ligatio, et fluxis actibus homo implicatur, dum non perfecte mundum deserit, dum non districto studio, sed dissolutis gressibus vadit, ut qui pro amore carnali parentum ad ea quae Dei sunt praepeditur
headnotes.en: … entangled, while he does not perfectly forsake the world, while he goes not with strict zeal but with dissolute steps, as one who for carnal love of parents is hindered from the things that are God's

headnotes.la: …eticorum (quorum figura sunt amici Job) non eget, id est, carnali sapientia; et recta, quae contra diabolum de conversione aliquando loquuntur, audire ab eis renuit, quia per haec ad perfidiam trahunt
headnotes.en: …e), that is, of carnal wisdom; and it refuses to hear from them even the right things which they sometimes speak against the devil concerning conversion, because through these they draw men to perfidy

headnotes.la: Quia non vobis in me stultitia sonat, si a vestra conscientia non procedat; sic Ecclesia prius falsa hostium destruit, post vera aperit, quibus non est locus dum falsa pro veris habentur; per
headnotes.en: …does not proceed from your own conscience; so the Church first destroys the false things of her enemies, afterwards opens the true, for which there is no place while false things are held for true; by

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Anima, est intentio mentis, etc., *usque ad*
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] The soul is the intention of the mind, etc., *as far as*

headnotes.la: …na a se habere glorietur, tentatione concuti permittitur, ut altitudo Dei et sui infirmitas videatur, sicut Salomon post sapientiam tentatur a meretricibus; haec tota hac mortalitate homo patitur unde
headnotes.en: …lf, he is allowed to be shaken by temptation, that the height of God and his own weakness may be seen, as Solomon after his wisdom is tempted by harlots; all this man suffers in this mortality, whence

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Saliva in os a capite labitur, etc., *usque ad* qui hoc vult mereri, fatetur malum quod fecit
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] Spittle slips into the mouth from the head, etc., *as far as* he who wishes to merit this confesses the evil which he has done

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Quasi: quid in recompensationem tibi offeram non invenio, quia omnis virtus hominis ad culpam abluendam infirma est. Vel,
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] As if to say: I find not what I may offer thee in recompense, because every strength of man is too weak to wash away guilt. Or,

headnotes.la: quasi ipsi in luce, Ecclesia sit in nocte: quam vocant, ut per cognitionem Dei surgat, et per precem poenitentiae praeterita diluat,
headnotes.en: …though they themselves were in the light, and the Church were in the night: which they summon, that it may rise through the knowledge of God, and through the prayer of penitence wash away things past,

headnotes.la: aliquando moraliter docent ex praeteritis praesentia conjici, scilicet ex transitu eorum quod haec nulla sint, unde subdit,
headnotes.en: sometimes they teach morally that present things are to be inferred from things past, namely from their passing, that these are nothing; whence he adds,

headnotes.la: …a omnis caro fenum [n: (Isa. XLVIII)]; qui arescunt, quia eorum opera cum carnis vita deficiunt. Sed hypocritarum ante: quia mox bona deserunt, ut ea consecuti sunt, propter quae simulaverunt. Hi sunt
headnotes.en: … together with the life of the flesh. But those of the hypocrites wither before: because they forsake good things as soon as they have obtained the things for the sake of which they feigned. These are

headnotes.la: …nim quae agit occulta cogitatione laudes quaerit, palam habens quod hostes praedentur. Ut Ezechias, qui post multa beneficia sibi facta, nuntiis regis Babylonis omnia sua bona ostendit: unde mox audit
headnotes.en: …den thought, having openly that which his enemies may plunder. As Hezekiah, who after many benefits done to him showed all his goods to the messengers of the king of Babylon: whence he presently hears

headnotes.en: …alignant are hypocrites, who do not even do good things well. Or, because outwardly they show themselves to their neighbour pure and simple, while inwardly they hide duplicity; against whom Moses says
that is, the mind with the joy

headnotes.en: …, to whom the person speaking is displeasing, attack all that he says, whether crooked or right; but Job, to whom not the person but the fault is displeasing, seeing that Baldath had said right things

headnotes.en: He does not trust in justice, but flees to prayer: who, even if I shall have had anything just, being fearful about that very prayer, says

headnotes.en: …s branches the bitterness which it drew from the root. These things also spiritually of Job, who both, fearing, foresaw the scourges of God in the whirlwind, and, foreseeing, bore them; whence he says

headnotes.en: [n: ( Ibid. )] That the heart is established is not in this place, etc., *as far as* he subjoins to him, as though teaching

headnotes.en: [n: (GREG.)] When the just man has begun to sink through outward evils also, then his brightness begins: on the contrary, the light of the wicked is in the day of this life, their darkness at evening

headnotes.en: He who thinks that he goes before all men in reason exults that he alone is a man

headnotes.en: …, and yet leaves them in their own unbelief, and those whom he had left in the fall of unbelief he at some time led back to the faith, and when they are thus restored there comes to pass what follows,

headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] But by that very loss of justice man dies, he is stripped of the garment of innocence granted in paradise, he is consumed, the destruction of the flesh following

headnotes.en: …ade thin by fear of the judge, and if they find in themselves any carnal thoughts, they consume them by the burning of penance. But the spirit of the wicked grows thick through the swelling of elation

headnotes.en: Through the ascension; afterwards, because Judaea was stirred against the disciples, he adds

headnotes.en: …elf is bound the more strongly to the love of heavenly things. Knowing that eternal rewards shall not be wanting to good desires: since temporal goods are not denied even to depraved and double hearts

headnotes.en: The expectation of the just is Christ; whom they knew would come at some time, but they sought that he should come sooner: whence here is added, now

headnotes.en: Before the coming of the mediator Job was to descend into hell, etc., *as far as* the retribution was still awaited to be received in the rest of hell alone

headnotes.en: …aid against a holy one: *Light* he calls the prosperity of the present life. But the light of the impious is quenched, because the prosperity of a fleeting life is ended together with that life itself

headnotes.en: Sometimes we take darkness for sadness and light for joy. The light therefore is darkened in the tabernacle of the impious, because in his conscience the joy which had come from temporal things fails

headnotes.en: Because the powers of his malice, which he now exercises, punishment shall afterwards bind fast

headnotes.la: etc. Quia videlicet stringetur finis in peccato
headnotes.en: etc. Because, namely, the end shall be bound fast in sin

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] In terra pedica absconditur, cum culpa sub terrenis commodis occultatur, quatenus homo videat, quid concupiscere valeat, et tamen nequaquam videat, in quo culpae laqueo pedem ponat
headnotes.en: …(Ibid.)] A snare is hidden in the earth, when a fault is concealed under earthly advantages, so that a man may see what he can covet, and yet may in no wise see in what noose of fault he sets his foot

headnotes.la: Caro nostra infirmitas est. Robur autem, anima rationalis, quae in expugnandis vitiis resistere per rationem valet. Quae fame attenuatur, cum nulla interni cibi refectione pascitur
headnotes.en: Our flesh is weakness. But strength is the rational soul, which by reason can resist in the overcoming of vices. Which is made thin by hunger, when it is fed by no refreshment of inward food

headnotes.la: [n: (Idem.)] De tabernaculo fiducia ejus evellitur, quando perversus qui multa in hac vita paraverat, repentina morte dissipatur
headnotes.en: [n: (Idem.)] His confidence is plucked out of the tabernacle, when the perverse man who had prepared many things in this life is scattered by a sudden death

headnotes.la: …itur, cum de honore vitae praesentis ad supplicia aeterna damnatur. Sic de unoquoque iniquo loquitur, ut ad caput, id est diabolum vertatur, qui in Antichristo nomen extendet, quod nunc mali imitantur
headnotes.en: … is damned to eternal punishments. Thus he speaks of each wicked man, so that it may be turned to the head, that is to the devil, who in Antichrist shall spread out the name which the evil now imitate

headnotes.la: Quia tanta tunc signa demonstraturus, etc., *usque ad* metuunt tormenta quae vincunt
headnotes.en: Because being then about to show forth so great signs, etc., *as far as* they fear the torments which they overcome

headnotes.la: id est, corda electorum pavore ferientur: unde scriptum est.
headnotes.en: that is, the hearts of the elect shall be struck with dread: whence it is written.

headnotes.la: Id est, vosmetipsos redarguendos relinquitis, et me districtis sententiis increpatis
headnotes.en: That is, you leave your own selves to be reproved, and rebuke me with strict sentences

headnotes.la: … aequo judicio a Domino sit afflictus. Si enim vita ejus et flagella pensantur, non aequo judicio videtur afflictus: quia vero merita ejus ex flagellis cumulavit, Deus non injusto judicio Job afflixit
headnotes.en: …udgment. For if his life and his scourges are weighed, he seems afflicted not with an equal judgment: but because he heaped up his merits out of the scourges, God afflicted Job with no unjust judgment

headnotes.la: …uin diabolus vicit (in eo quod de beati viri culpa promiserat) quem Deus laudavit. Hoc non elatio, sed dolor extorsit. Bonus si in humili mente, exigente causa vel dolore, bona de se dicit, non peccat
headnotes.en: … fault of the blessed man) him whom God praised. This not elation but sorrow wrung out. A good man, if in a humble mind, the cause or the sorrow requiring it, says good things of himself, does not sin

headnotes.la: Qui enim ita percutitur, ut vires ejus superentur, non hunc Deus ut filium per disciplinam, sed ut hostem ferit per iram: unde et propheta
headnotes.en: For he who is so struck that his strength is overcome, him God strikes not as a son through discipline, but as an enemy through anger: whence also the prophet

headnotes.la: …i spiritus, qui exquirendis hominum moribus occupantur: qui viam sibi in afflictorum cordibus faciunt, quando inter adversa quae exterius tolerantur, cogitationes quoque pravas immittere non desistunt
headnotes.en: … busied in searching out the ways of men: who make themselves a way in the hearts of the afflicted, when amid the adversities which are borne outwardly they cease not to send in depraved thoughts also

headnotes.la: Id est sacerdotes, quorum origo in Dei servitio deputata, jam per officium in conditione tenebatur
headnotes.en: That is, the priests, whose origin, assigned to the service of God, was already through their office held in the condition of

headnotes.la: Levitarum animae sunt ad secreta tabernaculi, quasi ad interiora cubiculi familiarius servientes
headnotes.en: The souls of the Levites are as it were serving more familiarly at the secret places of the tabernacle, as at the inner parts of the chamber

headnotes.la: Quia a synagoga non est cognitus; unde et propheta
headnotes.en: Because he was not known by the synagogue; whence also the prophet

headnotes.la: Qui enim ut Dominus auditus non est, non possessor agri, sed
headnotes.en: For he who was not heard as Lord was believed to be not the possessor of the field but

headnotes.la: Servus Judaicus populus fuit, timore obsequens; quem collatis muneribus, quasi emissis vocibus, ad se ducere statuit, sed non respondit, quia digna opera donis ejus reddere contempsit
headnotes.en: …le was the servant, obeying out of fear; whom, by gifts bestowed, as by voices sent forth, he determined to lead to himself, but he answered not, because he scorned to render works worthy of his gifts

headnotes.la: Quia dum legisperiti Deum despicerent, eorum incredulitatem turba populi secuta est. Relictis sapientibus, pauperes et stultos venerat quaerere: unde cum augmento doloris dicit
headnotes.en: …hile the men learned in the law despised God, the crowd of the people followed their unbelief. Leaving the wise, he had come to seek the poor and the foolish: whence with an increase of sorrow he says

headnotes.la: pro quibus ergo stultitiam suscepi, Verbum caro factum, despiciebant me
headnotes.en: they therefore for whom I took up folly, the Word made flesh, despised me

headnotes.la: Scribae et legis doctores, etc., *usque ad* de eodem legis doctorum ordine sequitur
headnotes.en: The scribes and the doctors of the law, etc., *as far as* concerning the same order of the doctors of the law there follows

headnotes.la: Piorum est cum ab adversariis patiuntur, non tam ad iram quam ad preces moveri. Tactum autem se manu Domini appellat, sicut ipse Satan dixerat
headnotes.en: It belongs to the godly, when they suffer from adversaries, to be moved not so much to anger as to prayers. And he calls himself touched by the hand of the Lord, as Satan himself had said

headnotes.la: Tanto Deus justius aliena vitia percutit, quanto in se nihil habet vitiorum. Et est sensus: Ita me ex infirmitatibus meis affligitis, ac si ipsi more Dei de infirmitate nihil habeatis
headnotes.en: … God strike the vices of others, as he has in himself nothing of vices. And the sense is: You so afflict me out of my weaknesses, as if you yourselves, after the manner of God, had nothing of weakness

headnotes.la: …iendo malitiam exercet. Vel, quasi non infirmi, qui non deberent increpare cum Deus percutit, ne addant dolorem dolori, sed consolari. Cum vero manus Domini cessat, tunc dignis increpatio potest fieri
headnotes.en: …ough they were not weak, who ought not to rebuke when God strikes, lest they add sorrow to sorrow, but to console. But when the hand of the Lord ceases, then rebuke can be made to those who deserve it

headnotes.la: …REG.)] Caro nostra post resurrectionem eadem erit et diversa. Eadem per naturam, diversa per gloriam. Eritque spiritalis, quia incorruptibilis et palpabilis: quia non amittet essentiam veracis naturae
headnotes.en: … resurrection shall be the same and diverse. The same by nature, diverse by glory. And it shall be spiritual, because incorruptible and palpable: because it shall not lose the essence of a true nature

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Faciem gladii fugere, est animadversionis districtae sententiam prius quam appareat, placare
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] To flee the face of the sword is to appease the sentence of strict animadversion before it appears

headnotes.la: [n: (GREG. in Job., l. XV.)] Ac si dicat: quia extremi judicii terrorem considero, idcirco cogitationum tumultibus in timore confundor
headnotes.en: [n: (GREG. in Job., l. XV.)] As if he should say: because I consider the terror of the last judgment, therefore I am confounded in fear by the tumults of my thoughts

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Quibus moderate praemissis, etc., *usque ad* et hoc invenio quod
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] These things having been moderately set down first, etc., *as far as* and this I find, that

headnotes.la: … hic illicita servavit desideria, nec in morte consumetur, sed ut sine fine crucietur, vivere sine fine compellitur, ut cujus vita hic mortua fuit in culpa, illic ejus mors vivat in poena. Dicat ergo,
headnotes.en: …ed in death; but that he may be tormented without end, he is compelled to live without end, so that he whose life was here dead in fault, there his death may live in punishment. Let him say therefore,

headnotes.la: Quasi nondum hypocrita, si cum hominibus de vita mea agerem, non timerem: quibus si displicerem, non curarem; sed quia cum Deo, merito tristor
headnotes.en: As if: not yet a hypocrite, if I were dealing with men concerning my life, I should not fear: and if I displeased them, I should not care; but because it is with God, I am rightly saddened

headnotes.la: Quis hoc vel desipiens sentiat, quod Deus ex timore nos arguat, et ex metu contra nos judicium suum proponat?
headnotes.en: Who, even doting, would think this, that God reproves us out of fear, and out of dread sets forth his judgment against us?

headnotes.la: Dicunt haeretici plebes, etc., *usque ad* pro peccatis dicunt retribui ei? Et hoc est,
headnotes.en: Heretics call the peoples, etc., *as far as* they say that it is repaid to him for sins? And this is,

headnotes.la: Per terram infirmitas actionis, per silicem fortitudo signatur, per torrentes aureos doctrina intimae claritatis. Ad se ergo conversis pro terra dat
headnotes.en: By earth is signified the weakness of action, by the flint strength, by the golden torrents the doctrine of inward brightness. To those therefore who are turned to him he gives for earth the

headnotes.la: Non elatus comparat se auro, sed sua humiliter considerat, quod licet omni justo. Et hoc est
headnotes.en: Not being lifted up does he compare himself to gold, but he humbly considers his own things, which is allowed to every just man. And this is

headnotes.la: Explet in me voluntatem suam, quia multis me percussionibus affligit. Sed
headnotes.en: He fulfils his will in me, because he afflicts me with many strokes. But

headnotes.la: Nunquam secura sunt corda justorum, sed turbata timore judicis, quae tamen consolantur donis quae acceperunt, unde
headnotes.en: Never are the hearts of the just secure, but troubled with the fear of the judge; which hearts nevertheless are comforted by the gifts they have received, whence

headnotes.la: Vultus humani cordis est similitudo Dei, quem perversus operit, ut cognosci a districto judice nequeat cum vitam suam malis actibus confundit, unde dicet
headnotes.en: …e of the human heart is the likeness of God, which the perverse man covers, that he may not be able to be known by the strict judge, when he confounds his own life with evil deeds; whence he shall say

headnotes.la: Cum enim justos ad regendae potestatis viderint culmen erumpere, perturbantur. Hi gaudent de dejectione bonorum, sed
headnotes.en: For when they see the just break forth to the summit of governing power, they are troubled. These rejoice at the casting down of the good, but

headnotes.la: id est, si ad regimen veniunt boni,
headnotes.en: that is, if good men come to rule,

headnotes.la: Per lunam Ecclesia, per stellas singulorum bene viventium animae designantur: qui culpas subigere perfecte desiderant. Sed quousque corruptione carnis astringuntur, ejus vinculis ligantur,
headnotes.en: … the souls of the several men living well are designated: who desire perfectly to subdue their faults. But so long as they are constrained by the corruption of the flesh, they are bound by its chains,

headnotes.la: [n: (Ibid.)] Terrae nomine Ecclesia designatur, etc., *usque ad*
headnotes.en: [n: (Ibid.)] By the name of earth the Church is designated, etc., *as far as*

headnotes.la: Sunt qui adversa patientes, Deum esse non credunt: nonnulli Deum esse aestimant, sed res humanas minime curare. Iste in typo Ecclesiae positus in afflictione, ut Deum esse fateretur, ait
headnotes.en: …s, do not believe that God is: some judge that God is, but that he by no means cares for human affairs. This man, set in the figure of the Church in affliction, that he might confess that God is, says

headnotes.la: Ut vero res humanas curare eum perhiberet, subdit
headnotes.en: And that he might declare that he cares for human affairs, he adds

headnotes.la: Solent haeretici de justitia gloriari, et catholicos fuisse iniquos criminantur. Contra quos per humilem confessionem dicitur
headnotes.en: Heretics are wont to glory of justice, and they accuse the Catholics of having been wicked. Against whom it is said, by way of humble confession

headnotes.la: Quia cum sit invisibilis, etc., *usque ad*
headnotes.en: Because, since it is invisible, etc., *as far as*

headnotes.la: Quia ab invisibili patre nascitur, etc., *usque ad*
headnotes.en: Because it is born of the invisible Father, etc., *as far as*

headnotes.la: …asi diceret Si Deum times, constat quia sapientia plenus es quae apud hominem timor Domini vocatur. Sed quia ille vere vim divini timoris intelligit, qui se ab omnibus pravis operibus custodit, subdit
headnotes.en: … is agreed that thou art full of the wisdom which among men is called the fear of the Lord. But because he truly understands the force of divine fear who keeps himself from all depraved works, he adds
The tabernacle, a dwelling, etc., *as far as*

headnotes.la: Sanctae Ecclesiae interiora effervescere, etc., *usque ad* et hoc est,
headnotes.en: That the inward parts of holy Church boil up, etc., *as far as* and this is,

headnotes.la: [n: (GREG.)] Sciens se videri cavet, non tamen securus et perfectus quidem inter veteres, in praeceptis futuri Christi pensat, quam multa de perfectione minus habet. Ideo dicit
headnotes.en: …EG.)] Knowing himself to be seen he takes heed, yet not secure and perfect indeed among the ancients, he weighs in the precepts of the Christ to come how much he lacks of perfection. Therefore he says

headnotes.la: Qui judicari cum servis suis ancillisque non renuit, etc., *usque ad* unde et protinus subdit
headnotes.en: He who refuses not to be judged together with his menservants and maidservants, etc., *as far as* whence also he forthwith adds

headnotes.la: Lunam dicit famam, quae lucens in nocte hujus vitae ex bono opere vires accipit
headnotes.en: By the moon he means fame, which, shining in the night of this life, receives its strength from good work

headnotes.la: Si, inquam, hoc vel illud feci, etc., *usque ad* de illis ergo,
headnotes.en: If, I say, I did this or that, etc., *as far as* of them therefore,
